instructions: Cut the potatoes into 1 inch chunks. Peel 8 oz of the carrots and cut them into 1/2 inch pieces. Put both in a large pot, cover with cold water and add 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Bring the pot to a boil over high heat, then turn it to medium and cook for 10 minutes, until a knife slides into the potato with no push.
Add 1 cup of the peas and cook for 1 minute.
Drain everything in a colander, then spread it on a baking sheet. Leave it for 15 minutes, until it's cool to the touch.
Meanwhile, finely dice a quarter of the red onion and drain the tuna.
In a large bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, olive oil, vinegar, black pepper and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Add the cooled vegetables, the tuna and the onion. Fold gently, so the potatoes stay in pieces.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt, or a splash of the vinegar.
Cover and chill for at least 1 hour. It keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Stir it before you pack a portion, and don't freeze it.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
advance_prep_notes: chill at least 1 hour before eating, or make it up to 3 days ahead
method_notes: No version showed 20 or more ratings, so this is a fallback; the lead is the best-rated one read (4.34 from 3 votes, visible rating). Saveur and one other page blocked or gave no rating, so only two versions were read. Both agree on boiled potato and carrot, peas, oil-packed tuna and mayonnaise; the Spanish Chef adds egg, olives and cornichons and makes its own mayonnaise. I left out egg and olives and used jarred mayonnaise to keep the effort lunch-sized.
